findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion tying each shard to its projected line-recovery (or a stated minimum), so the headline ~2,033-line goal is measurable at close.
evidence: Body: 'Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970...'
Body: 'runner.py 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot...)'
No AC references line count, comment-line reduction, or per-shard recovery targets
findings.finding: The plan's headline deliverable — recovering ~2,033 lines and restoring headroom on named hotspots (runner.py 3 → ~48, etc.) — has no covering acceptance criterion; all six ACs measure process (shards land, lists appended, ADRs written, stale comments corrected) rather than the line-recovery outcome the whole rationale rests on.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all six) vs. body 'Total recoverable: ~2,033 lines' / 'Headroom recovered where it is tightest'
scenarios: A shard lands having appended its do_not_move list and written ADRs but recovers far fewer lines than projected — every AC passes yet the stated goal is missed
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Each shard reduces src comment lines by at least [per-shard target], verified by diff line-count; net recovery across shards ≥ ~2,000 lines.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the specific ADRs to be written (per shard) so AC4 has a fixed, checkable list rather than an approximate '~13'.
evidence: Body: '~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times'
Only one ADR is described concretely ('one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize...')
'~13' is approximate, so 'all proposed ADRs written' has no fixed denominator
findings.finding: AC4 requires 'Proposed ADRs are written' but the plan only states '~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards' and enumerates a single example; the specific ADR set the executor must author is not listed, leaving the criterion unmeasurable and the scope undefined.
findings.location: AC4 'Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations' / body '~13 new ADRs are proposed'
scenarios: Executor writes 9 ADRs and declares AC4 done; a reviewer cannot tell whether the other ~4 were required
findings.suggested_fix: List each proposed ADR title/subject in the plan (or reference the shard artifact that enumerates them) and change AC4 to 'Each ADR in [list] is written'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword AC6 to a checkable form, e.g. 'No comment enumerated in any shard's do_not_move list is deleted or altered', anchoring the invariant test to the appended tools.md lists.
evidence: AC6: 'No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant'
'load-bearing' is a judgement term; the AC states no check tying it to the do_not_move lists
findings.finding: AC6 'No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant' relies on the subjective term 'load-bearing invariant' with no deterministic verification procedure, making it hard to evaluate in-session beyond the do_not_move lists.
scenarios: Reviewer disputes whether a deleted comment was 'load-bearing'; no objective test resolves it
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC6 to: 'No comment appearing in a shard's do_not_move list (as appended to .joe-janitor/tools.md) is removed or weakened by that shard's edits.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to every ADR-producing child (4b94, 4fc1, ab77, ad16, da4c) an acceptance criterion that each proposed ADR/amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that cites it is collapsed (destination-first), matching 9ce8's superseding AC.
evidence: Parent AC4: 'Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations'.
Only 9ce8's superseding ACs add: 'Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed or deleted — destination first, then the relocation'.

4b94 proposes a web-search capabilities ADR; 4fc1 proposes 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation'; ab77 proposes 'Three new ADRs from review_bot/'; ad16 proposes 'Three new ADRs'; none of these five children's ACs restate 'ADR written' or 'destination-first ordering' — their AC1 only says 'relocated or deleted per its destination' which names but does not require the destination to pre-exist.
9ce8 CORRECTION §2 itself articulates the risk: 'If a comment citing "see ADR NNNN" is collapsed before ADR NNNN exists, the citation dangles and the argument is simply LOST'.
findings.finding: Parent AC4 ('Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations') is covered as a before-collapse ordering guarantee for ONLY the reconciler child; the five other children that propose ADRs carry no acceptance criterion that the ADR exist/be committed before the citing comment is collapsed.
scenarios: A shard (e.g. 4b94) collapses a capabilities.py block to 'see ADR 00XX' but the ADR is not yet written/committed, leaving a dangling citation and lost argument — the exact failure the reconciler child guards against but the other five do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate 9ce8's 'destination first, then the relocation' AC to all children that propose ADRs, and add a parent-level AC that no citation is introduced to a non-existent ADR.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to each child an acceptance criterion that any history block citing no ticket has a ticket FILED before that block is reduced/collapsed.
evidence: Parent AC3: 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first'.

Every child's AC set is: 'relocated or deleted per its destination' / 'do_not_move appended' / 'verified-stale corrected' / 'no load-bearing invariant lost' — none states the file-a-ticket-first precondition as an outcome.

ad16 BODY (not AC) notes 'two are costly: untracked follow-ups in production_batch_runner.py that must be filed first'; 4b94 BODY notes '85 lines are free wins — history already citing b690...'. These are prose covering only two children's instances, not roster acceptance criteria and not scope-matching the parent clause across all shards.

9ce8's superseding AC 'nothing is deleted without a destination that already exists' is the closest, but it is scoped to the reconciler child and frames destinations as ADRs, not ticket-filing for uncited history.
findings.finding: Parent AC3's second clause — 'history citing none has a ticket filed first' — is not restated as a measurable acceptance criterion by ANY sibling in the roster; no child AC asserts that a ticket must exist before an uncited history block is collapsed.
scenarios: A child collapses an uncited history block to a citation of a ticket that was never filed, so the history is lost rather than relocated — with no child AC to catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a shared child AC: 'History citing no ticket has a ticket filed and committed before the inline block is reduced to its citation.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the parent body's '~970 / 28 sites' reconciler figures (and the '~2,033' total) with 9ce8's re-measured '~12 occurrences across 10 files', marking all such counts as measured-outputs not targets.
evidence: Parent body: 'Per shard: reconciler ~970 ...' and '28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM ..."'.
9ce8 CORRECTION: 'The real figure is ~12 occurrences across 10 files, not 28' and 'That estimate is therefore UNRELIABLE and must not be treated as a target.'
9ce8 superseding AC: 'The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the unreliable ~970 estimate.'
findings.finding: Conflicting assumption between the parent plan body and the reconciler child (9ce8): the parent asserts the reconciler yields '~970' lines from '28 sites' of the RELOCATED-VERBATIM/800-cap marker, but 9ce8's own superseding CORRECTION re-measures this as '~12 occurrences across 10 files' and declares '~970' an UNRELIABLE estimate that 'must not be treated as a target'.
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer treats the parent's ~970 as the reconciler shard's target and manufactures relocations to hit it — the exact anti-pattern the child forbids.
The parent's aggregate '~2,033 lines' total is built on the repudiated ~970, so the parent's headline yield is itself unreliable.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the parent body to cite the corrected reconciler baseline (or drop hard numbers), and label the per-shard/total figures as estimates that are outputs of the work.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare the append protocol for the shared .joe-janitor/tools.md (append-only, section-per-shard, or serialized landing order) so concurrent shard appends cannot conflict or overwrite.
evidence: Every child AC2: 'The shard's do_not_move list is appended to .joe-janitor/tools.md BEFORE any edit lands.'
Parent AC2 mirrors this per-shard but names no coordination for the shared target file.
Six shards land separately (parent AC1) but the roster gives no ordering among them beyond ad16 depends_on 4b94.
findings.finding: Implicit shared state: all six children append their do_not_move lists to the SAME file '.joe-janitor/tools.md', but no child (nor the parent) specifies an ordering or merge discipline for these concurrent appends across siblings.
scenarios: Two shards land in overlapping windows and both edit .joe-janitor/tools.md, producing a merge conflict or an overwrite that drops one shard's protection record.
A later-landing shard's append is rebased over an earlier one and silently drops entries, defeating the 'so a future sweep does not re-flag them' purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parent-level note that each shard appends under its own shard-id heading and that tools.md changes are append-only, or serialize the six shards' landing order.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Carry the parent's signing.py negative result into ab77: record that signing.py recovers only ~5-8 lines, its comments are security invariants (do_not_move), and any real split is out of scope.
evidence: Parent body: 'signing.py (798) recovers ~5-8 ... Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants ... those splits are out of scope here.'
ab77 scope: 'root-level src/rebar/*.py plus attest/, metrics/, review_bot/, ...' — signing.py is a root-level src/rebar/*.py, so it falls in ab77's scope.
ab77 body discusses _mcp_models, _mcp_llm, _config_schema, review_bot ADRs — but never signing.py; the negative result the parent asserts is not carried by the owning child.
By contrast da4c explicitly carries the parallel negative result for its two files (event_append.py, _processors.py).
findings.finding: Owned-by-none / consistency gap for signing.py: the parent body names signing.py (798 LOC, recovers ~5-8, comments ARE security invariants) as one of the three files comment-triage cannot fix, but the child that owns root-level src/rebar/*.py (ab77) never mentions signing.py or carries its negative result.
scenarios: An implementer of ab77 attempts to trim signing.py's security-invariant comments to hit a line target because the child plan gives no negative-result guidance, risking loss of a load-bearing security invariant the parent flagged.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a signing.py negative-result note plus a do_not_move entry to child ab77, mirroring da4c's treatment of event_append.py/_processors.py.
